rationale: The candidate is a coherent early massing with a readable dominant bar-like volume and a courtyard/void condition that is generally aligned to the neighborhood-living brief. The blue frontage edge is answered by an open seam/void rather than a sealed face, which is the right direction. In all four views the same basic solid-and-void logic remains legible, so it clears the hard pass, but the form is still somewhat box-like and the section is not yet especially articulate for public ground or daylight. The top view and oblique views agree well enough to support the same spatial idea, and the reference set reinforces that a compact low-rise mass with a carved court and occasional bridging/terracing is the right family. I would preserve the dominant courtyard gesture and improve section/public-threshold expression rather than radically re-typologizing it.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact low-rise mass with a carved central void and strong horizontal datum; good precedent for a neighborhood building with a legible public threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger and more campus-scaled than the candidate; do not copy the tower/podium scale.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like clustering around a courtyard suggests how to keep one dominant void while varying support masses.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more transparent and landscape-embedded than the candidate.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated low-rise composition with a central atrium/courtyard and site-responsive plan; useful for active-ground, horizontal neighborhood massing.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is more sectional and landscape-driven; candidate is more compact and box-like.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, connected wings and bridging elements can produce a clear public sequence without losing compactness.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More complex than candidate; avoid over-fragmentation if adapting this principle.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes with a central void and upper-level bridging are directly transferable to strengthen hierarchy and public space.

warnings: The mass still reads as a fairly generic rectilinear extrusion with a cutout, so stronger profile or sectional articulation would help.
The courtyard is legible, but its publicness could be more emphatic at the access edge.
Avoid over-fragmenting the solid; the current hierarchy should remain one dominant body with one primary void.
